# Tropical cove — shared A/B/C base Run with Node 22: ```sh npm ci --cache /tmp/beach-npm-cache npx vite --port 5191 --strictPort node scripts/shoot.mjs A ``` Open `http://localhost:5191/?group=A&cam=wide`. Fixed views are `wide`, `beach`, and `closeup`; omit `cam` for mouse/touch OrbitControls. `?time=4` freezes water animation for repeatable comparisons. All screenshot runs use the same time, 1280×720 viewport, specified Chromium executable, and SwiftShader flags. ## Built - Three.js Water with planar reflections, locally generated repeating normal map, animated fine normals and small geometric swells, sun specular glitter, depth-based turquoise-to-blue absorption, procedural seabed ripples and animated caustics, and broken shoreline foam. - A shared analytical shoreline controls terrain, wet sand, foam and water depth. Sand has dune relief, a raised berm, filtered wind-ripple normals, and a roughly three-metre dark, low-roughness wet band with an analytical sky-reflection tint. Seeded shells, pebbles and seaweed follow the high-tide debris line. Rocky ridges, dark canopy and a right-hand headland belong to the shared landscape, outside the prop slots. - Procedural tropical-blue sky with soft cumulus, warm afternoon directional sunlight and hemisphere fill, ACES tone mapping, restrained bloom, atmospheric haze, and shadow support for future props. - Eight empty `THREE.Group` markers preserve each slot's exact id and position. `src/props.js` exports `loadProps(group)`, `propRoot`, and one empty A function per slot in `slotStubs`. - B/C use `slot.paths.B` / `slot.paths.C` in `assets/props.json`, load with GLTFLoader, normalize bounding-box height, center X/Z, and place the minimum Y at the analytical ground height. Paths point to `assets/tripo/.glb` and `assets/library/.glb`. - Vite production builds copy the assets directory, including future GLBs, into `dist/assets`. ## Visual iterations Four wide-view checkpoints record three screenshot → correction → screenshot cycles. All use the original camera coordinates and frozen time 4. | Checkpoint | Review and subsequent fixes | | --- | --- | | `shots/base_r1.png` | Excessive terrain ridge, beach camera below sand, washed-out water. Capped shoreline curvature, lowered dunes, reduced reflection/light contribution. | | `shots/base_r2.png` | Broad bloom washed out the coast; uniform foam; regular sand ripples. Reduced bloom and bounded reflected radiance, broke up foam, varied ripples and filtered the normal map. | | `shots/base_r3.png` | Far terrain boundary visible, water too flat, sand too gray-green. Extended terrain with a nonuniform grid, added small swells and fine wave normals, warmed sand and lighting. | | `shots/base_r4.png` | Final shared base. Distant boundary removed, turquoise depth gradient readable, warmer sand. | Final camera images: `shots/A/wide.png`, `shots/A/beach.png`, `shots/A/closeup.png`. Props deliberately remain absent, so the fixed closeup is mostly empty sand until later groups are implemented. ## Shared base polish — round 2 Three additional screenshot → review → fix rounds used the unchanged wide and beach cameras, 1280×720 and frozen time 4. Each checkpoint also has a corresponding `shots/base2_rN_beach.png`. | Checkpoint | Review and subsequent fixes | | --- | --- | | `shots/base2_r1.png` | Added dunes/berm, wet band and tide debris, rolling breakers, blue sky, ridged island and right headland. Ripples were too strong and canopy too spherical/dark; reduced and distance-filtered ripple normals, shrank and increased canopy clusters, broke up foam lines. | | `shots/base2_r2.png` | Sand relief became subtler and surf readable. Sun glare was excessive, foliage material multiplied its instance colors too dark, and clouds were stretched; bounded glitter, corrected canopy color multiplication and replaced cloud patches with rounded cumulus. | | `shots/base2_r3.png` | Clouds were oversized and canopy still too coarse. Reduced cloud size, increased smaller canopy clusters, warmed wet sand, increased water-normal frequency for finer mid-distance detail and tightened visible glitter. | | `shots/A/{wide,beach,closeup}.png` | Final captures after the third correction, regenerated with the original `node scripts/shoot.mjs A`. | `src/props.js`, `assets/props.json`, cameras and all existing scripts are unchanged. Shared terrain still supplies the loader's analytical ground height. Landscape/debris geometry lives outside `propRoot`; all eight A slots remain empty. ## Verification - `npm run build` passes. Vite reports a nonblocking bundle-size advisory for the three.js bundle. - `node scripts/shoot.mjs A` passes for all three cameras with no browser or shader errors. - `node scripts/verify.mjs` passes: intercepts B/C asset requests with an in-memory offset test mesh, verifies all eight heights, horizontal centers and ground contacts for both groups; also verifies empty A slots, advancing wave time, and mouse-driven OrbitControls. The fixture is never saved into the asset directories. - Real B/C GLBs were not supplied. Loader failures retain their empty markers and report warnings/results; the screenshot script treats browser resource errors as failure after saving the views, so missing assets cannot silently qualify as a successful group capture. ## Known weaknesses - Water is an efficient analytical approximation, not a fluid simulation. The visible sandy bottom and caustics are evaluated inside the Water shader rather than through a refractive scene-depth buffer; submerged props will not refract correctly. - Foam animates along a fixed shoreline; it does not physically advance over the sand. Swells are small, with planar reflection approximations. - Landforms and canopy are procedural approximations; individual foliage clusters remain discernible. Sand and caustic patterns can reveal repetition at close range. Wet sand uses an analytical sky-colored Fresnel approximation, not a second planar reflection pass. - Bounding-box grounding uses the slot center's ground height. Very wide future props may need per-asset adjustments to avoid local dune intersections. Animated/compressed GLB extensions have not been tested. - SwiftShader captures prioritize reproducibility, not real-device frame-rate measurement. ## Group A All eight slots now contain code-generated three.js models. `src/props.js` dispatches the A builders in `src/props-a.js`, batches geometry by material, and normalizes each model to the exact configured height, horizontal slot center, and analytical ground height. Slot markers retain the exact `pos` values from `assets/props.json`. Seeded geometry, canvas grain/chipped-paint maps, and a procedural basalt shader are the only asset sources: no model files, image assets, remote requests, or CDNs are used by A. B/C loading behavior is unchanged. The shared `src/main.js`, water, sky, sand, lighting, post-processing, cameras, and slot configuration are unchanged. | Prop | Approach | Triangles | | --- | --- | ---: | | `palm_tall` | Curved, tapered tube trunk with growth rings and crown sheaths; 15 arched fronds made from separate tapered leaflets; seven coconuts. | 17,088 | | `palm_pair` | Two individually seeded palms with different heights and opposing leans from a shared base. | 30,288 | | `rocks` | Seven irregular, smoothed basalt meshes, separately grounded; vertex color variation and shader pores; ray-placed open barnacle shells with dark apertures. | 25,340 | | `boat` | Hollow tapered hull with seven blue strakes per side, separate inner wood surfaces, ribs, floorboards, three thwarts, gunwales, nails, oarlocks, and two stowed wooden oars. | 15,600 | | `hut` | Short stilts, braces, individual floor/wall planks, doorway, side windows, steps, and seven overlapping courses of irregular palm thatch. | 9,896 | | `umbrella` | Timber pole and radial ribs under layered straw thatch; two slatted loungers with raised backs, armrests, legs, support struts, and bolts. | 9,788 | | `driftwood` | Curved irregular bleached trunk, longitudinal grooves, tapered broken branches/root forks, end faces, and splinters. | 7,192 | | `lifeguard` | Splayed white supports and cross braces, elevated plank deck, railings, ladder, lookout seat, red plank roof, rescue cross, and lifebuoy. | 1,868 | Total: **117,060 triangles**, counted from the final mesh geometry, excluding the shared scene and inspection floor. Counts are also saved in `shots/A/props/triangles.json`. ### Isolated inspection With the development server running, open `http://localhost:5191/props.html?solo=boat` (substitute any slot id). This independent viewer uses a neutral grey background/floor, fixed studio lights, and a fixed three-quarter camera. Each model is uniformly scaled so its longest bounding-box dimension is three units; all use the same camera, ground baseline, 38-degree field of view, and 800×800 capture. This exposes the natural aspect-ratio differences rather than stretching narrow props. These studio settings do not affect the beach comparison. ```sh node scripts/shoot.mjs A node scripts/shoot-props.mjs node scripts/props-contact.mjs r4 node scripts/verify.mjs npm run build ``` Scene captures: `shots/A/{wide,beach,closeup}.png`. Individual renders: `shots/A/props/.png`. The contact-sheet utility uses local Python/Pillow solely to arrange verification screenshots; its output is never loaded as a scene asset. ### Three correction rounds | Checkpoint | Review and corrections | | --- | --- | | `shots/A/r1.png` | Initial complete set. Lounger backs tilted downward; rocks were excessively faceted; driftwood ends were open; thatch looked like regular wooden pickets. | | `shots/A/r2.png` | Round 1: corrected lounger back rotation, smoothed/refined rock topology, closed driftwood ends with splinters, widened palm leaflets, lowered protruding hut posts, and replaced broad regular thatch with finer, denser, varied strips. | | `shots/A/r3.png` | Round 2: tapered and curved the driftwood with forked branches, added basalt pore shading, cut hut windows, added individual tower roof boards and thatch course relief. Batched meshes by material to reduce draw calls. | | `shots/A/r4.png` | Round 3 plus final grounding review: irregular drooping thatch edges, open barnacle apertures and denser colonies, gentler driftwood branch taper, boat nails/oarlocks, lounger bolts, and a corrected transform reset after batching. Grounded each rock separately before assembling the cluster. Final scene and individual captures were regenerated. | ### Verification and remaining weaknesses - `node scripts/shoot.mjs A` and `node scripts/shoot-props.mjs` complete without browser or shader errors. - `node scripts/verify.mjs` now checks populated A slots as well as the B/C fixture loaders: all eight heights, horizontal centers, and ground contacts match within `1e-5`. Live water animation and OrbitControls remain operational. - `npm run build` passes; Vite retains its nonblocking large-bundle advisory. - Palm foliage and straw remain thin ribbon approximations, with no wind animation or subsurface scattering. Thatch still has an underlying conical silhouette, and palm crowns can look sparse at distance. - Wood grain is procedural and repeated; it is not anatomically correct end grain on every face. The boat's strakes are thin surfaces and its underside is simplified. Driftwood forks are still visibly constructed at close inspection. - Rock pores are shader detail rather than fully modeled cavities; barnacles repeat a small shell profile. - The unchanged shared shadow map produces fine self-shadow patterns on small lounge slats and foliage. Large props are grounded at the slot's central terrain height, so individual feet can intersect uneven sand. The isolated viewer removes terrain variation but does not conceal those scene limitations. ## Explore mode Open **http://localhost:5191/?explore=1&group=A** and press **點擊開始**. Explore is explicitly opt-in: a URL without `explore=1` retains OrbitControls; any `cam` parameter takes precedence and retains the original comparison view. The explore module and CSS load only in explore mode. Shared water, sky, terrain, lights, prop generators, fitting rules, and existing screenshot scripts are unchanged. - WASD / arrows move relative to the camera; mouse looks around; Shift runs; Space jumps. V toggles third/first person. Esc releases pointer lock and pauses; click the start button to resume. While paused, the group buttons remain accessible. - 1 / 2 / 3 or the segmented buttons switch A｜codex 程序化, B｜Tripo, C｜免費素材庫 in place. The HUD counts actual mesh triangles, excluding the landscape and avatar. Missing files leave empty slots and a visible missing count. Near loaded props, a label identifies the slot and source. - M or the sound button mutes procedural wave/wind audio, created only after the initial click. P freezes the player and camera and hides the HUD; P again returns. Touch users can tap the lower-right corner to leave photo mode (the exit control is invisible until hovered/focused so captures remain clean). - Touch devices have a left joystick, right drag-to-look region, jump button, view toggle, group buttons, and photo control. - Ground contact uses `groundHeight()`. Water deeper than 0.65 m is blocked, shallow wading slows movement and emits pooled splash rings, and the cove is bounded at X −34…35 and Z ≤27. Expanded world-space slot boxes stop the player and shorten the third-person camera boom. Camera height is clamped above sand. A newly switched model that surrounds the player permits movement toward an exit without teleporting the player. Implementation: `src/explore.js` and `src/explore.css`, with a small opt-in hook in `src/main.js`. Character geometry is shared, ten splash meshes are pooled, camera vectors are reused, collision boxes are built only after loading, and POI text changes only when its target/group changes. Group loads are serialized and up to three groups are cached to prevent repeated GPU allocation on revisits. The existing loader and its fitting rule remain untouched. ### Screenshot / feel iterations 1. `shots/explore/round1/`: initial screenshots showed an oversized character, high camera pitch, and floating-looking feet. Pulled the follow camera farther back, lowered its angle, added shoes and head shadows, and added a small walking bob. Kept paused HUD controls reachable after pointer unlock. 2. `shots/explore/round2/`: reviewed the improved walk views. Smoothed limb return when stopping, shortened source labels, and fixed the group-switch overlap case so a player can exit newly overlapping bounds. Final captures are `shots/explore/{start,walk1,walk2,group_switch}.png`; `mobile.png` checks the portrait touch layout. ### Verification - `node scripts/shoot-explore.mjs`: same Chromium executable and SwiftShader flags as `shoot.mjs`; uses `?auto=1` to bypass pointer lock after clicking start, steps a reproducible scripted path, saves all four required captures, checks movement, A/B/C switching and retained position, V, photo freeze, deep-water limits, and camera height. The automation API exists only with `auto=1`. - `node scripts/verify-explore.mjs`: passed jump, boat collision, forced 404s for all eight B assets, rapid C→A switching, hidden photo HUD, and touch joystick movement. Missing-file checks use request interception, leaving actual assets untouched. - `node scripts/shoot.mjs A`: passed all three views. Pillow RGB image differences against pre-change backups were empty for **wide, beach, and closeup**: pixel-identical, not merely the same framing. - `npm run build`: passed, with the existing nonblocking three.js chunk-size advisory. ### Known issues - AABB prop collision is deliberately conservative: palm foliage and open hut/umbrella space can block walking. This is a lightweight exploration controller, not mesh-accurate physics; jumping does not implement traversable prop platforms. - Group geometry is cached for the page lifetime. Reload to pick up newly generated GLBs or retry previously missing files. The first switch may pause movement while assets decode; cached revisits reuse models. Large supplied GLBs can still be expensive. - SwiftShader verification cannot establish 60 fps on a physical desktop GPU. The controller avoids per-frame object creation, but actual rendering throughput depends on the unchanged base scene and supplied prop complexity. No real-GPU performance claim is made. - Character animation and audio are procedural approximations. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults. license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt --- # Frontend Design Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified. ## Ground your designs in the subject matter If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout. ## Design principles For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option. Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct. Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif. Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page: - Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color. - Using all caps for labels. - Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content. Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence. Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed. Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance. ## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits: 1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell); 2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; 3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns; 4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration; 5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text. All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn. Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles. - Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values. - Type: the typefaces and their roles. - Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified? - Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique. Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan. When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections. ## Restraint and self-critique Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes. ## More on writing in design Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience. Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever. Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around. Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act. Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

## Hub & compare

- **Hub:** "'`http://localhost:5191/` presents A｜codex 程序化, B｜Tripo AI, and C｜免費素材庫, links to Explore and the solo viewer, and a synchronized comparison entry. Thumbnails come from `shots/<group>/beach.png`; absent thumbnails show「生成中」. `/report/stats.json` contains `{groups:{A:{minutes,cost,triangles,notes},B:{...},C:{...}}}` with null numeric placeholders. Fill these values to publish real statistics; cost may be a currency-qualified string. Nothing is estimated from placeholder data.
- **Scene:** the original scene entry is now `/scene.html`. `?cam=`, `?group=`, `?explore=1`, `?time=`, and automation flags retain their behavior. Legacy root URLs containing `cam`, `group`, or `explore` redirect with the complete query/hash preserved. Screenshot and verification scripts now use the explicit scene entry.
- **Comparison:** `/compare.html?groups=A,B` supports any two groups or all three. A single scene, renderer, camera, water clock, avatar, and Explore controller are shared. Props load serially through the unchanged singleton loader, are cached, and toggle visibility per pane. The existing bloom/output pipeline renders at pane resolution; an offscreen composite presents all scissored panes together to avoid a transient blank pane after resizing. Landscape geometry/materials, lights, water/sky/sand, and postprocessing settings are unchanged. The picker changes groups in place, retaining player position and orientation. Collision bounds combine the selected groups, so all panes follow one movement path. Group labels show the number of missing models as「生成中」. Esc pauses pointer lock so the picker is reachable; touch Explore controls are retained.
- **Solo:** `/props.html?group=A&solo=boat` offers group/prop selectors, OrbitControls, and an actual mesh triangle count (including instance multiplicity). Missing models show「生成中」without throwing. Models retain the existing longest-dimension = 3 units normalization, baseline, 38° FOV, and initial `(4.6,3.3,5.8)` camera aimed at `(0,1.25,0)`. Switching groups disposes previous GPU resources. `scripts/shoot-props.mjs` adds `capture=1` to hide the UI and retain the original 800×800 capture behavior.
- **Build:** Vite now builds all four HTML entries and copies report data and available group thumbnails alongside scene assets.

### Validation and visual review

- `node scripts/verify-ui.mjs` passes: 1440×900 hub/comparison/solo, 390×844 hub viewport without horizontal overflow, synchronized movement, picker changes retaining player location, solo selection, forced GLB 404s in both solo/comparison, and legacy URL redirection. Screenshots: `shots/ui/{hub,compare_AB,compare_ABC,solo}.png` plus full-page `shots/ui/hub_mobile.png`. All five were visually reviewed. The initial three-pane resize capture exposed a blank pane; composing the complete frame before display fixed it.
- `node scripts/shoot.mjs A` passes. RGB image differences against pre-task backups are empty for **wide, beach, and closeup**: pixel-identical framing and rendering.
- `node scripts/shoot-props.mjs A boat` passes; its RGB difference against the original boat capture is also empty.
- `node scripts/verify.mjs` passes. Its outdated exact-height-only assertion was updated to respect the already-existing height/maxLen caps: both bounds must hold and one must be reached. Prop implementations and fitting rules were not changed.
- `npm run build` passes with the existing nonblocking large-chunk advisory.

Comparison caches all three prop groups for fast switching. Missing GLBs are retried on reload. Rendering costs grow with pane count because reflections, shadows, and bloom still run per pane, while base geometry/material allocations remain shared. SwiftShader checks establish rendering correctness, not a measured physical-GPU frame rate. B assets are being generated independently; missing counts and available thumbnails can change as that work completes.
EOF
